references.text: Continuation of the same thought: it is not because of Israel's righteousness that they receive the land, but because of the wickedness of the nations and the Lord's promise to the fathers.
The Lord did not choose Israel because they were a great people, but because of his love and the promise to the fathers—not because of any merit of their own.
Warning against thinking that one's own power and strength have brought wealth—a parallel thought about not taking credit for God's gifts.
The sin of the Amorites was not yet complete—showing that the driving out of the peoples was tied to their wickedness, not Israel's righteousness.
The nations who lived in the land before Israel were driven out because of their sins and abominations.
God's choice is not based on works, but on his own will and grace—a parallel to the idea that Israel did not deserve the land.
Salvation is by grace, not by works—the same principle as that Israel did not receive the land because of their own righteousness.
Salvation is a gift from God, not something to boast about—the same theological principle that blessing does not come from one's own merit.
